description:
Overview

The University of the South Pacific (USP) opened applications on 13 November 2026 for full-time Masters and PhD scholarships under the Pacific–European Union Marine Partnership (PEUMP II). The scholarships support research in fisheries management, governance and policy, ocean ecosystems, and data and technology. Awardees begin their studies in Semester 1, 2027 at USP’s Laucala Campus in Suva, Fiji.

This is a genuinely fully funded package: tuition, a monthly living allowance, a research grant, book and dependent allowances, and travel support are all included. It is open only to citizens of the 15 PEUMP Pacific Island countries.

Funding and Duration

PEUMP II scholarship benefits (official USP figures)
ItemDetails
Tuition and feesFull tuition fees, general service fees and health services fees, paid directly to USP.
Living allowanceFJD 1,787.50 per month.
Book allowanceFJD 375 per semester.
Dependent allowanceFJD 906.80 per month, under USP dependent’s allowance criteria.
Establishment allowanceFJD 1,942 one-off, for qualifying awardees who relocate.
Research grantFJD 20,000, released once the research proposal is approved by the Research Committee.
Travel allowanceUp to FJD 2,000 for qualifying awardees.
DurationPhD: 3 years. Masters: 2 years. Full-time only.

Research Themes

  • Fisheries Management: offshore and coastal fisheries management, the Parties to the Nauru Agreement, climate impacts on fisheries livelihoods.
  • Governance, Policy and Blue Economy: tuna governance (WCPFC), marine policy, co-management and customary marine tenure, ocean finance, blue economy entrepreneurship.
  • Ocean, Ecosystems and Climate: climate adaptation, ecosystem-based management, mangrove and seagrass restoration, ocean currents and reef-passage monitoring.
  • Data, Technology and Food Security: fisheries statistics, data science and AI, eDNA monitoring, marine spatial planning, value chains, seafood safety and cold-chain improvements.

Eligibility

Who can apply
ItemDetails
NationalityOnly citizens of the 15 PEUMP Pacific Island countries: Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Nauru, Niue, Palau, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu, Papua New Guinea and Timor-Leste.
AdmissionYou must meet USP’s postgraduate admission requirements for the Masters or PhD programme you choose.
Study modeFull-time only.
EmploymentPaid employment is not allowed during the tenure of the award (contributing to teaching at USP’s Centre for Sustainable Futures may be possible).

Application Dates

Key dates
ItemDetails
Applications open13 November 2026.
Application deadline4 January 2027.
Award commencementSemester 1, 2027.
Contactimr@usp.ac.fj (Institute of Marine Resources).

How to Apply

  • Review the PEUMP II research themes and example topics, and identify the theme that best fits your background.
  • Confirm your eligibility — citizenship of one of the 15 PEUMP countries and USP postgraduate admission requirements.
  • Prepare your CV, certified academic transcripts and certificates, contact details of two referees, and a short statement of research interest naming your preferred theme.
  • Email the completed application to imr@usp.ac.fj before 4 January 2027. Incomplete applications are not accepted; only shortlisted candidates are contacted for interview.

Official Link

USP — Pacific European Union Marine Partnership (PEUMP II) Scholarship

Important Notes

  • This scholarship is only for citizens of the 15 PEUMP Pacific Island countries — applicants from elsewhere are not eligible.
  • Awardees may not hold paid employment during the scholarship tenure.
  • The FJD 20,000 research grant is released after research-proposal approval — a strong proposal matters as much as grades.
  • Applications close on 4 January 2027; incomplete applications are rejected.
